title: [Performance][Ops] Skip invisible KPool page-table loads
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Main-branch counterpart of #18576, carrying the same two-file minimal change.

In the int32 paged-cache scoring path, the final tile may contain pools that are within configured capacity but beyond the query's actual visible prefix. Key loads already use the visibility mask, while block-table loads previously used only the capacity mask.

Use the existing `valid = (pools < max_pool_seq_len) & (pools < visible)` mask for block-table loads as well. This is the only production behavior change: invisible pool lanes no longer perform page-table reads. Valid-input scores and selected token indices are expected to remain unchanged.

The final diff contains only this mask change and boundary cases added to the existing eager/graph regression test. No helper extraction, wrapper reorganization, new benchmark/compilation-audit scripts or documentation expansion is included.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API, serving flag, score formula or output-layout change. Dense score allocation and `torch.topk` remain capacity-wide. This patch does not resolve 1M-capacity scratch/TopK overhead, and no isolated end-to-end speedup has been established for this mask-only change.

### How was this patch tested?

- Local Python syntax, repository-pinned Ruff check/format and whitespace checks passed.
- Full local `bash format.sh ci` was attempted but actionlint environment installation failed on this Windows host. Full CI remains pending.
- Extend the existing paged scoring and causal-tail regression with capacities 127/128/129 around the 128-pool tile boundary, in both eager and graph modes. The existing replay step also shortens visible lengths and checks selection, tail and padding against the CPU reference.
- Target NPU validation remains pending in the requested separate environment; previous full-model performance and GSM8K smoke results are not validation of this reduced revision.

```bash
pytest -q tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_glm5next_pool_key_indexer_triton.py
```

#### Related full-model ITL comparison

For **4K input / 2K output** (4096 / 2048 tokens), the author-reported mean ITL improved from approximately **116 ms to 96 ms**, a reduction of **20 ms (17.2%)**.

| Input tokens | Output tokens | Mean ITL before | Mean ITL after | Reduction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4096 | 2048 | ~116 ms | ~96 ms | ~17.2% |

These figures describe the earlier full-model dense-serving optimization. They are performance context, not a controlled before/after measurement of this PR's reduced page-table mask change; target-runtime validation of this revision remains pending.

AI assistance: Codex assisted with implementation and PR preparation.
